questions.stem: On Analogous harmony: a designer reviewing a nonprofit annual report notices that a designer uses three neighboring hues from the color wheel. What character does this scheme usually have?

options.text: The maximum possible contrast between all three colors
options.misconception: mistakes neighboring hues for opposing complementary hues

options.text: A strictly monochromatic single-hue result with no variation
options.misconception: confuses several adjacent hues with just one hue

options.text: A calm and unified look with subtle variation between hues
An unpredictable clash with no underlying relationship
options.misconception: denies the clear relationship that defines the scheme

questions.explanation: An analogous scheme uses colors adjacent on the color wheel, producing a harmonious and calm effect with gentle variation. Unlike complementary pairs, the chosen hues are closely related, so the overall result feels unified and quietly coherent.
questions.hint: Are the chosen hues neighbors on the wheel or opposites?
